words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) does more than add another item. It governs {{ar:ٱلْيَوْمِ}} ({{tr:al-yawmi}}) as a sworn-by genitive object, while also tying 85:2 back to the oath in 85:1 and forward to the next oath member in 85:3. Because the particle is rootless and bound, its force comes from attachment: the oath act is compressed into one prefixed sign, fused in recitation with the definite day, so the ayah opens as a second solemn beat rather than as a detached statement.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins in oath mode before the day is explained, so the phrase functions as sworn evidence rather than ordinary narration.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the prefixed particle as available for oath government, and the following noun is genitive as the particle complement.

topics.headline: second oath beat in a chain

topics.reason: The word has no root or independent inflection, and the local surface joins it directly to the definite noun it governs.

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْيَوْمِ}} ({{tr:al-yawmi}}) is not a loose adverbial "on a day." The oath particle governs it in genitive case, and its article makes the sworn object a recognizable day that is then narrowed by {{ar:ٱلْمَوْعُودِ}} ({{tr:al-mawʿūdi}}). The root can name ordinary day-length, but the modifier pulls the noun toward event-time: one bounded appointed occasion, not time in general. That makes the wording different from naming the day by recompense in 1:4 or by resurrection in the oath formula of 75:1; here the day is known through prior promise. In the phrase's sound, the shorter {{ar:ٱلْيَوْمِ}} ({{tr:al-yawmi}}) opens into the longer {{ar:ٱلْمَوْعُودِ}} ({{tr:al-mawʿūdi}}), so the promised adjective is heard as an expansion of the day rather than as a detached label. Within the oath sequence, 85:1 moves from ordered sky to this definite time, and 85:3 can then turn the promised time toward witness-language.

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمَوْعُودِ}} ({{tr:al-mawʿūdi}}) makes promise an adjective of the day itself. It agrees with {{ar:ٱلْيَوْمِ}} ({{tr:al-yawmi}}), shares its oath-governed genitive case, and arrives after the noun so the phrase first names the day and then lands on its promised status. The passive participle makes the day the pledged object while leaving the promiser and recipients off the surface; the certainty is carried by the form rather than by a full clause. The root field can include threat and appointment, so the word is narrower than an overt threat noun but heavier than simple reassurance: the promised day feels like a fixed appointment. Its longer closing cadence expands the sound material of {{ar:ٱلْيَوْمِ}} ({{tr:al-yawmi}}), lets the oath rest on guarantee, recalls truth-promise language (21:97; 30:6), and prepares the matching passive witnessed form in 85:3.

topics.headline: promise qualifies the day
topics.summary: The definite genitive participle agrees with the day noun and functions as its postposed adjective.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that promise is not a separate object beside the day; it is the condition by which the sworn day is identified.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the word as an adjective of the definite genitive noun, and QAC marks matching definiteness and genitive case.

topics.headline: day as pledged patient
topics.summary: The passive participial form makes the day the promised object while omitting promiser and recipient from the compact surface.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees guaranteed status foregrounded over the mechanics of who promised to whom.
topics.reason: The local form is a passive participle with no attached recipient phrase; it compresses a recoverable promised-day clause into an adjective.

topics.headline: promise range charged by appointment
topics.summary: The root's threat and appointment branches remain as pressure, while the local form stays a passive promise adjective rather than a threat noun or appointment noun.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses guaranteed futurity as both fixed appointment and possible warning, without mistaking the word for an explicit threat label.
topics.reason: V4 supports promise, threat, and appointed-time branches for the root; the local passive participle preserves promisedness and narrows the other branches to latent color.

topics.headline: truth-promise certainty compressed
topics.summary: Cross-surah truth-promise passages clarify the certainty carried here by the adjective without making truth an explicit local word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the word's certainty as part of the wider promise-that-does-not-fail frame (21:97; 30:6), even though 85:2 keeps the wording compressed.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows supply concrete references to 21:97 and 30:6; these function as echoes of reliable promise, not as replacements for the local adjective.

topics.headline: ending lands on guarantee
topics.summary: The final passive adjective closes the ayah with a longer, heavier cadence so promisedness is the acoustic landing point.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the oath rest finally on pledged status, not merely on the noun for time.
topics.reason: The word is the ayah-final modifier, and the sound-level observations match its local position after the shorter day noun.

topics.headline: promised becomes witnessed
topics.summary: The passive participle shifts the oath sequence from visible stations to guaranteed time and prepares the matching witnessed passive form in 85:3.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader follows a sequence in which what is guaranteed in 85:2 is set up to become witnessed in 85:3.
topics.reason: The local word is a passive participle at the oath boundary, and the CRITICAL rows give the concrete forward comparison with 85:3.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **One appointment carrying promise and threat at once.** `ي و م` B003 supplies a severe event-day, while `و ع د` B001 allows a promise concerning good or harm and B002 specifies threat. The later paired outcomes, burning punishment (85:10) and gardens (85:11), supply the two directions; I infer that one appointed event distributes them. The “promised day” therefore remains simultaneously assurance for the harmed and menace for the perpetrators.

2. **A fixed rendezvous, not vague futurity.** `و ع د` B003 supplies an appointed time or place. The later pair “He initiates and returns” (85:13) and the preserved text (85:21-22) make fulfillment structurally repeatable and secured. I infer that a promise preserved and backed by the power to return events cannot dissipate into indefinite expectation. The ayah reads as a scheduled convergence of witness, deed, and requital.

3. **The day already signaled by the packet.** `و ع د` B006 supplies a promising sign of an expected state. The sky, witness-pair, fire, contrasting destinations, and encompassing closure form a sequence of signs. The packet supplies those images; I infer their prospective direction toward the named day. Thus “promised” can describe not only prior speech but a day whose approach is legible in the present signs.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The adjacent pair of outcomes in 85:10-11 is the decisive surprise: one موعد holds both `و ع د` B002 threat and B001 promise without requiring a compromise between them. The initiation/return pair of 85:13 makes the appointment dynamic, and the guarded tablet of 85:22 makes it durable. These later relations correct a vague future reading; the day is an event toward which preserved testimony and effective return are already ordered.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **An appointed crisis, not a neutral date.** Lexical evidence: `ي و م` B003, “an event-day or severe occasion”; `و ع د` B002, “a threat directed toward harm,” and B003, “an appointed time or place.” Structural cue and role: witness/witnessed in 85:3 opens onto killing, trench, fire, and the perpetrators’ own witnessing in 85:4–7. Those later details furnish a severe case awaiting an appointment. Abductive move: I infer that the witnessed violence is what makes the appointed day a crisis of requital; the causal link is not stated in 85:2. Reading change: `اليوم الموعود` carries both scheduled certainty and threatening pressure rather than only futurity.

2. **The promise already has signs.** Lexical evidence: `و ع د` B006, “a promising sign of what is expected.” Structural cue and role: the sky’s ordered `بروج` in 85:1 and the witness/sign pair in 85:3 stand on either side of `الموعود`. They make the surrounding world function as present indication of the future appointment. Abductive move: I infer that the flanking oath objects are signs of fulfillment rather than merely co-listed objects. Reading change: the promised day is read as anticipated by visible markers now, not as an unsupported remote claim.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 85:7 made the appointment newly forensic: the perpetrators’ self-witnessing gives the severe-event branch of `ي و م` B003 a concrete case. It also corrected the “promising sign” reading of `و ع د` B006 from a merely celestial omen into evidence pointing toward reckoning.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Faith, Promise, and Denial

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Promise creates an object of assent, while disbelief and accusation reverse the same epistemic relation by refusing or discrediting what is offered as true.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A person or community binds itself to a sacred object through worship, assent, praise, promise, fidelity, repentance, and pardon.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Testing, Ordeal, and Crisis

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, gözle görülür belirtilerden toprak, gün, hayvan veya insan hakkında gelecek bir durumun beklenmesini ortaklaştırır. Beklenen şey her zaman iyilik değildir; günün başlangıcı sıcaklık ya da soğukluk gösterebildiği için çekirdek, olumlu umut yerine belirtiye dayalı gelecek beklentisi olarak kurulmalıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Genel niteleme ile toprak, gün, hayvan ve insan belirtilerine bağlı kuruluşlar ayrı örnekler olarak korunur; bunlardan sözlü söz verme anlamı çıkarılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir varlıkta veya durumun başlangıcında görülen belirtilerin, gelecekte ortaya çıkacak bir özellik ya da sonuç için beklenti doğurmasıdır. Toprağın yağmur ve bitki, günün sıcaklık veya soğukluk, hayvanın gelişme, insanın da huy bakımından değerlendirilmesi bu çekirdeğin farklı gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Şimdiki belirtiler, gelecekte ortaya çıkacak bir durum, özellik veya sonuç için beklenti doğurur.
Topraktaki belirtiler, ileride yağmur alınacağı ve bitki yetişeceği umudunu doğurabilir.
Günün başlangıcı, ilerleyen saatlerde sıcaklık veya soğukluk görüleceğini gösterebilir.
Bir hayvanın belirtileri, ondan iyilik veya olumlu gelişme bekleneceğini gösterebilir.
Bir insanın görünür belirtileri, cömertlik, dayanıklılık veya kararlılık gibi huyların beklendiğini gösterebilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, mevcut belirtilerden geleceğe ilişkin bir durum beklenmesi çekirdeğinde birleşir; toprak, gün, hayvan ve insan bu beklentinin farklı taşıyıcılarıdır.
